_read_me: A form, not a dataset. Copy it, replace every value, delete what you do not use.
Each value is: requirement | type | what goes here.
Two separate ground truths per question, and keeping them apart is the point:
relevant_corpus_documents is what retrieval should find; expected_answer is what should be said.

groundtruth_dataset_metadata.name: mandatory | string | Human-readable title, e.g. Support tickets 2025 — questions.

corpus_ref.dataset: mandatory | string | The corpus id these questions were written against. Must equal that corpus's dataset field.
corpus_ref.file_fingerprint: optional, strongly advised | 16 hex characters | Which version of that corpus. An id says which corpus; only this says which version, so a corpus edited after the questions were written is caught instead of silently mis-scored.

groundtruth_dataset_metadata.language: optional | string | Only when the questions are not in the corpus's language.
groundtruth_dataset_metadata.description: optional | string | What this question set covers.
groundtruth_dataset_metadata.generated_at: optional | date-time | When the questions were written.
groundtruth_dataset_metadata.excerpt_note: optional | string | Present only in a sample.
groundtruth_dataset_metadata.default_question_asked_at: mandatory once any question says last month or similar | date-time | The now that a relative time phrase resolves against. Without it the same question has a different right answer every day.

question_metadata_fields._note: mandatory once any question carries labels | object | Same shape as the corpus's label_fields, with applies_to: [question]. Descriptive only: nothing the scoring branches on lives here.

<your_question_label>.type: mandatory | string | As in the corpus's label_fields.
<your_question_label>.description: mandatory | string | What this label means.

glossary.<allowed_value>: optional | string | What this value means.

evidence_role_values._note: mandatory once any evidence carries a role | object | Declare only the roles you use.
evidence_role_values.supporting: optional | string | The evidence supports the expected answer.
evidence_role_values.contradicting: optional | string | The evidence contradicts the question's premise.
evidence_role_values.current: optional | string | States the latest value of a fact that changed.
evidence_role_values.superseded: optional | string | States an earlier value of that same fact.
evidence_role_values.context: optional | string | Needed to read the others, answers nothing alone. Never use it on the only evidence for a claim.

groundtruth_dataset.groundtruth_question_id: mandatory | integer >= 1 | Unique in this question set.
groundtruth_dataset.question: mandatory | non-empty string | Exactly as someone would put it to the system. This is the retrieval query; nothing else in this file may be handed to retrieval.

expected_answer.behavior: mandatory | one of answer, abstain, correct_premise | What the system should do. answer: answer from the corpus. abstain: say the corpus does not contain it. correct_premise: the question asserts something false, so correct it. Whether the question is answerable follows from this and is not stored twice.
expected_answer.text: mandatory unless behavior is abstain | string | One correct answer in prose, in the corpus's language. Two of the four judged metrics are computed against it, so leaving it out costs half the decision.

derived_facts.derived_fact_id: mandatory | integer >= 1 | Unique in this question. Evidence points at it by this number.
derived_facts.fact: mandatory | string | One claim a correct answer must contain. One claim each: never join two with and, because each is evidenced separately.

relevant_metadata.<label_name>: optional | matches its declared type | The corpus labels this claim rests on. A claim about when something happened rests on your date label.

relevant_corpus_documents._note: mandatory list, may be empty | list | Empty when behavior is abstain: nothing in the corpus answers it. At least one entry otherwise.
relevant_corpus_documents.corpus_document_id: mandatory | integer >= 1 | A document in the referenced corpus.

evidence.text: mandatory | non-empty string | What this piece is. Read together with fidelity, which decides what the string is.
evidence.fidelity: mandatory | one of verbatim, paraphrase, computed | verbatim: copied character for character, and checked to be findable. paraphrase: your words for something the document does say. computed: a fact worked out from a label, never written in the text, as a date resolved from a timestamp. Neither of the last two is checked for a verbatim match, which is why this cannot be omitted.
evidence.role: optional, mandatory once two pieces must be told apart | string | What it does for the answer. Must be declared in evidence_role_values.

document_metadata.<label_name>: optional | matches its declared type | Every label the document carries, copied whole, not just the relevant ones. A label that looks irrelevant when the question is written may be what a retriever matched on, and a selection made in advance cannot be reconsidered later. Must equal what the corpus holds.

part_labels.<part_label_name>: optional, mandatory on verbatim | matches its declared type | The labels of each part this text lies in, in order. A list because a quote may run across two. Empty on computed, whose text lies in no part.

relevant_metadata.<label_name>: optional, mandatory on computed | matches its declared type | Of the labels above, the ones this piece rests on. On a computed piece it is the label the fact was worked out from, and the only place that is recorded.

supports: optional, mandatory once the question has 2+ derived_facts | list of integers | The derived_fact_ids this piece carries. Absent means it supports the answer as a whole.

relevant_metadata.<label_name>: optional | matches its declared type | Which of this document's labels would let a filter find it. A different question from the same field on a piece of evidence, which says what that piece rests on.

question_metadata.<label_declared_in_question_metadata_fie: optional | matches its declared type | e.g. difficulty, question_type. Descriptive only: nothing here changes a score, and nothing here may be handed to retrieval unless the system predicts it itself.
